summary: Implemented an Internet Identity-based login page and updated some UI branding to “CloudCam AI”. Added backend auto-creation of a basic user profile record. However, the diff summary does not provide clear evidence that protected-route redirects (/dashboard, /camera) are enforced, and backend persistence/permissions for user profiles across upgrades and for first-time authenticated users is not fully evidenced. Significant unrequested Stripe billing and other feature work also appears to have been added.

missing_requirements.requirement: Require authentication (Internet Identity) for feature pages (at minimum: Dashboard and Camera) and redirect unauthenticated users to /login.
missing_requirements.reason: The diff summary references route protection in frontend/src/App.tsx, but no actual App.tsx diff content is included to verify redirects for /dashboard and /camera or behavior after logout.
evidence: frontend-file-summaries.txt (mentions protected routes in frontend/src/App.tsx, but without code)

missing_requirements.requirement: Ensure a basic user account record is created and persisted for each authenticated principal the first time they use the app (principal, createdAt, tier), safe to call multiple times.
missing_requirements.reason: Backend shows an in-memory Map-based ensureUserProfile, but the provided snippet does not show stable storage or upgrade-safe persistence for userProfiles. Additionally, getCallerUserProfile requires an AccessControl #user permission, but the diff does not show how authenticated principals are granted #user so first-time users can successfully trigger auto-creation.
evidence: backend/main.mo (userProfiles declared as `let userProfiles = Map.empty...`; ensureUserProfile uses userProfiles.get/add; getCallerUserProfile requires AccessControl #user)

missing_requirements.requirement: Update all user-facing product name/branding text to consistently say “CloudCam AI”, replacing inconsistent references (e.g., “CloutChem AI”).
missing_requirements.reason: User-facing text appears updated in several places, but the diff still includes prominent references to `cloutchem` assets in Header and Landing page. While filenames may not be user-visible, the diff summary does not demonstrate a complete audit/removal of inconsistent branding references across the UI.
